topIssues.title: op-reth: ships zero default bootnodes for OP Stack chains; cannot bootstrap discv5 without --bootnodes
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
## Summary

`op-reth` (in this monorepo at [`rust/op-reth/`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/tree/559c958d0746670420398195bd605c5c2055f02f/rust/op-reth)) ships **zero hardcoded P2P bootnodes for any OP Stack chain**. A fresh node started with `--chain optimism`, `--chain base`, or any other OP chain gets an empty discv5 bootnode list from the chainspec and cannot bootstrap unless the operator passes `--bootnodes` (or sets it in a config file, or supplies `--trusted-peers`).

This is a behavioural regression vs `op-geth`, which auto-applies a built-in OP-Stack bootnode pool to any chain selected via `--op-network`.

## Evidence

`OpChainSpec::bootnodes()` is a pure delegation to upstream `reth-chainspec`:

https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/559c958d0746670420398195bd605c5c2055f02f/rust/op-reth/crates/chainspec/src/lib.rs#L290-L292

```rust
fn bootnodes(&self) -> Option<Vec<NodeRecord>> {
    self.inner.bootnodes()
}
```

Upstream `reth-chainspec` is pinned in [`rust/Cargo.toml`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/559c958d0746670420398195bd605c5c2055f02f/rust/Cargo.toml#L313-L322) at `paradigmxyz/reth` rev `27bfddeada3953edc22759080a3659ccea62ca1f`.

At that rev, `ChainSpec::bootnodes()` ([`crates/chainspec/src/spec.rs#L782-L792`](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/27bfddeada3953edc22759080a3659ccea62ca1f/crates/chainspec/src/spec.rs#L782-L792)) handles only Ethereum L1 chains:

```rust
pub fn bootnodes(&self) -> Option<Vec<NodeRecord>> {
    use NamedChain as C;
    match self.chain.try_into().ok()? {
        C::Mainnet => Some(mainnet_nodes()),
        C::Sepolia => Some(sepolia_nodes()),
        C::Holesky => Some(holesky_nodes()),
        C::Hoodi   => Some(hoodi_nodes()),
        _ => None,
    }
}
```

There are no `OP_BOOTNODES`/`op_nodes()` constants at this rev — [`crates/net/peers/src/bootnodes.rs`](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/27bfddeada3953edc22759080a3659ccea62ca1f/crates/net/peers/src/bootnodes.rs) is a single-file Ethereum-only module.

Network startup pulls bootnodes via:

https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/559c958d0746670420398195bd605c5c2055f02f/rust/op-reth/crates/node/src/node.rs#L1414-L1422

```rust
.discovery_v5(args.discovery.discovery_v5_builder(
    rlpx_socket,
    ctx.config()
        .network
        .resolved_bootnodes()
        .or_else(|| ctx.chain_spec().bootnodes())
        .unwrap_or_default(),
))
```

For any OP chain, layer 2 (`chain_spec().bootnodes()`) is `None`, so unless the operator supplies `--bootnodes` the discv5 bootnode set is empty.

Confirmed not extracted from the embedded superchain-registry tarball either — [`crates/chainspec/src/superchain/configs.rs`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/559c958d0746670420398195bd605c5c2055f02f/rust/op-reth/crates/chainspec/src/superchain/configs.rs) reads `genesis` and `ChainMetadata` (hardfork timestamps, chain id, batchInbox) only. Grepping the entire `superchain/` subtree for `bootnode|enode` returns zero matches.

## Comparison with op-geth

op-geth ships two static enode pools in [`params/bootnodes.go#L82-L111`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/blob/df72b4274e121aff5b5e96b15620404d505372c2/params/bootnodes.go#L82-L111):

- `V5OPBootnodes` — 11 enodes (3 OP Labs, 5 Base, 3 Uniswap Labs)
- `V5OPTestnetBootnodes` — 8 enodes (3 OP Labs, 2 Base, 3 Uniswap Labs)

Selection happens in [`cmd/utils/flags.go#L1407-L1422`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/blob/df72b4274e121aff5b5e96b15620404d505372c2/cmd/utils/flags.go#L1407-L1422):

```go
case ctx.IsSet(OPNetworkFlag.Name):
    network := ctx.String(OPNetworkFlag.Name)
    if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(network), "mainnet") {
        urls = params.V5OPBootnodes
    } else {
        urls = params.V5OPTestnetBootnodes
    }
```

`--op-network` accepts any chain in `superchain.ChainNames()` (the embedded superchain registry — ~60+ chains). Selection between mainnet/testnet pool is purely a substring `mainnet` check; there's no per-chain customization. Same generic pool for every OP Stack chain known to the registry.

## Comparison with the superchain-registry

The upstream `ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry` does **not** publish bootnode data per chain — verified by grepping `superchain/configs/` in the upstream repo. The registry's per-chain TOML files (`op.toml`, `base.toml`, `unichain.toml`, …) carry `name`, `public_rpc`, `chain_id`, `hardforks`, `genesis`, `roles`, `addresses` — no `bootnodes` field anywhere.

So a "read bootnodes from the registry" fix isn't just a wiring change in op-reth — it requires a schema extension to the registry first (and per-chain ownership to populate the data).

## Two paths forward

### Option A — Mirror op-geth's static pool (quick parity)

Replace the pure delegation in [`rust/op-reth/crates/chainspec/src/lib.rs#L290-L292`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/559c958d0746670420398195bd605c5c2055f02f/rust/op-reth/crates/chainspec/src/lib.rs#L290-L292) with a `match` that hardcodes the same V5OPBootnodes / V5OPTestnetBootnodes pool that op-geth ships, keyed off `Chain::is_optimism()` / `Chain::is_testnet()`:

```rust
fn bootnodes(&self) -> Option<Vec<NodeRecord>> {
    if self.inner.chain.is_optimism() {
        if self.inner.chain.is_testnet() {
            return Some(op_testnet_nodes());
        }
        return Some(op_mainnet_nodes());
    }
    self.inner.bootnodes()
}
```

with a small companion module under `rust/op-reth/crates/chainspec/src/` containing the two enode lists, copied from op-geth as the source of truth (the lists are intentionally cross-referenced — op-geth is canonical).

**Pros**

- Single-file change, fully self-contained in the monorepo.
- No upstream-reth or superchain-registry coordination.
- Achieves immediate behavioural parity with op-geth.
- Same generic-pool semantics op-geth already has (so users running op-reth get the same default, no better, no worse).

**Cons**

- Same coarse semantics as op-geth: one pool serves every OP Stack chain. Long-tail chains may not actually peer via these enodes.
- Duplicates op-geth's hardcoded list. Drift risk: if op-geth bumps the pool (e.g. when a sequencer rotates IPs), op-reth needs a manual sync.

### Option B — Add bootnodes to the superchain-registry schema (long-term)

1. Extend the registry's per-chain config schema with an optional `bootnodes` field (array of enode URLs).
2. Have chain operators populate it (OP, Base, Unichain, Worldchain, Zora, Mode, Ink, Fraxtal, Soneium, Celo, …).
3. Bump op-reth's vendored `chain_metadata.rs` to surface the field, and have `OpChainSpec::bootnodes()` return it when present, falling back to `inner.bootnodes()` otherwise.
4. Optionally retire op-geth's V5OPBootnodes lists in favour of the registry-driven list, with a transition window.

**Pros**

- Per-chain ownership: each chain operator controls its own bootnode list and can rotate without coordinating with EL clients.
- Single source of truth across op-geth, op-reth, and any future OP-Stack EL.
- Removes the OP-Labs / Base / Uniswap-only bias of the current static pool.

**Cons**

- Multi-repo, multi-team coordination: superchain-registry schema RFC, registry PRs from N chain operators, op-reth + op-geth wiring.
- Not blocking on this issue — Option A can ship first and Option B can land independently later.

## Recommendation

Ship **Option A** now to close the parity gap. It's a one-file, self-contained change with no external dependencies. Open a separate ecosystem RFC for Option B (registry schema + per-chain operator buy-in).

## Test plan

- Unit test: assert `OpChainSpec::for(Chain::optimism_mainnet()).bootnodes()` returns 11 enodes; same for `base`, `unichain`, `worldchain`, etc.
- Unit test: `OpChainSpec::for(Chain::optimism_sepolia()).bootnodes()` returns 8 enodes; same for sepolia variants of each chain.
- Smoke test: `op-reth node --chain optimism --discovery.disable-discovery=false` (no `--bootnodes`) connects to ≥1 peer within 60s on a fresh datadir.
- Compare bootnode lists byte-for-byte with op-geth's `params.V5OPBootnodes` to prevent drift.

## Verified against

- `ethereum-optimism/optimism` `origin/develop` @ `559c958d0746670420398195bd605c5c2055f02f` (2026-04-30)
- `paradigmxyz/reth` pinned rev `27bfddeada3953edc22759080a3659ccea62ca1f`
- `ethereum-optimism/op-geth` `origin/optimism` @ `df72b4274e121aff5b5e96b15620404d505372c2` (2026-04-28)
- `ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry` `main` (live, fetched 2026-04-30)

topIssues.title: op-supernode: simpleChainContainer.vn field accessed without synchronization
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
## Summary

The `c.vn` field on `simpleChainContainer` is a plain pointer accessed from multiple goroutines without mutex protection or `atomic.Pointer`. This is a data race.

## Details

**Writers:**
- `Start()` restart loop goroutine — assigns `c.vn` when creating a new VirtualNode

**Readers (from other goroutines):**
- `PauseAndStopVN()` — reads `c.vn` to call Stop
- `Stop()` — reads `c.vn` to call Stop
- `SyncStatus()` — reads `c.vn`

The flow control uses atomic bools (`pause`, `stop`) which create memory barriers, but there is a check-then-act window between setting the pause flag and reading `c.vn`. For example, in `PauseAndStopVN`:

```go
c.Pause(ctx)       // sets pause=true
if c.vn == nil {   // reads c.vn — but Start() may have just assigned a new VN
    return nil
}
return c.vn.Stop() // could be a different VN than what was checked
```

Between `Pause()` and the `c.vn` read, the restart loop can create and assign a fresh VN (line 212 in `Start()`), then see the pause flag and sleep. The caller then stops this new VN, but the loop can wake and create yet another.

## Why it hasn't caused failures yet

1. `VirtualNode.Stop()` is idempotent (internal mutex, returns nil if already stopped)
2. Go GC prevents use-after-free on the old pointer
3. The window is very small in practice
4. The restart loop checks pause immediately after VN creation

## Suggested fix

Protect `c.vn` with a `sync.Mutex` or use `atomic.Pointer[virtual_node.VirtualNode]` (Go 1.19+). The mutex approach is simpler since `Start()` already holds the only write path.

## Context

Found during review of #19571. The `Stop()` method has the same pre-existing pattern — `PauseAndStopVN` just inherits it. Not a regression, but worth fixing.

**File:** `op-supernode/supernode/chain_container/chain_container.go`

topIssues.title: op-reth: proofs init panics on nodes synced with reth v1 storage format
topIssues.author: dhyaniarun1993
topIssues.body:
## Description 

Running op-reth proofs init on a production OP Mainnet node panics with:

```
index out of bounds: the len is 1 but the index is 32
```

The panic originates in PackedStoredNibbles::from_compact (nibbles.rs:208), which reads buf[32] as the nibble count. On nodes that were first synced before reth introduced v2 packed storage, trie keys in the AccountsTrie MDBX table are stored in v1 format — 1 nibble per byte, variable length (1–64 bytes). A 1-nibble key is just 1 byte, so indexing buf[32] panics.

Root cause:
`InitializationJob::initialize_accounts_trie` hardcodes `tables::PackedAccountsTrie` (v2 codec, 33-byte keys) regardless of which format the reth node actually uses. Reth records the active storage format in its `Metadata` table under `storage_settings`. The init job ignores this, always applying the v2 codec to what may be v1 data.

topIssues.title: op-dispute-mon: ability to query supernode's VNs to get output roots
topIssues.author: pauldowman
topIssues.body:
The transition period for operators that run supernodes and op-dispute-mon will require running two instances of op-dispute-mon until the output root games have finalized. Currently, dispute-mon relies specifically on cl nodes to enrich FaultDisputeGames. And supernodes only to enrich SuperFaultDisputeGames. 

To simplify dispute-mon configuration and the infra around it, it would make sense for dispute-mon to query supernode's VNs to get output roots. This way one can run a dispute-mon that specifies only supernode-rpcs to monitor super and non-super dispute games.

topPRs.title: feat(op-reth): Proof store v2
topPRs.author: dhyaniarun1993
topPRs.body:
**Description**

This PR introduces MdbxProofsStorageV2, an alternate MDBX backend for the op-proofs subsystem that replaces the v1 versioned-value schema with `3-table-per-domain pattern` (current state + changeset + sharded history bitmap).

**Motivation**

The proof storage ExEx has two sync paths:
- Fast path: block updates arrive in real-time from the ExEx notification stream and are persisted directly.
- Slow path: used during catch-up, where the node re-executes blocks and recalculates state roots to reconstruct the proof data.

The primary motivation is improving slow-path throughput. One of the bottleneck in the slow path is state root calculation, which requires reading the current state of every modified trie node and account. In the v1 schema these are stored as versioned DupSort entries — reading the latest value requires seeking past all prior versions. Under v2, the current state table holds exactly one row per key, so every read during state root computation is a direct O(1) lookup, eliminating the version scan entirely.

**Tests**

`tests/lib.rs` and `tests/live.rs` refactored to `#[test_case]` parameterised tests — each scenario runs against inmemory, mdbx (v1), and mdbxv2 backends from a single test body.

Devstack: `op-reth-with-proof-v2` EL kind
`op-devstack/sysgo/mixed_runtime.go` and `tests/proofs/utils/preset.go` support a new `MixedL2ELOpRethV2` kind so integration tests can target the v2 backend via `OP_DEVSTACK_PROOF_VALIDATOR_EL=op-reth-with-proof-v2`.


**Metadata**

Blocked on https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19909

topPRs.title: chore(rust): bump reth to v2.2.0
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- Bumps reth from floating rev `27bfddeada` (~v2.1.0) to **v2.2.0** (`88505c7fcb`)
- Adapts to alloy-evm 0.34 / alloy-* 2.0.4 API changes
- Workspace `cargo check`, `clippy -D warnings`, and `cargo +nightly fmt --check` all pass

## Dependency bumps

| crate | old | new |
|---|---|---|
| `reth` (git rev) | `27bfddeada` | `88505c7fcb` (v2.2.0) |
| `reth-codecs` / `-codecs-derive` / `-primitives-traits` / `-rpc-traits` / `-zstd-compressors` | 0.3.0 | 0.3.1 |
| `alloy-evm` | 0.33.0 | 0.34.0 |
| all `alloy-*` (consensus/eips/rpc-types/network/...) | 2.0.0 | 2.0.4 |
| `alloy-eip7928` | 0.3.3 | 0.3.4 |
| `roaring` (lockfile only) | 0.11.3 | 0.11.4 |

`roaring` had to be bumped explicitly: reth v2.2.0's `IntegerList(RoaringTreemap)` derives `Eq`, and `RoaringTreemap: Eq` only landed in 0.11.4 (released 2026-04-24).

## Upstream API changes adapted

**`BlockExecutor::commit_transaction` is now infallible** (returns `GasOutput`, not `Result<GasOutput, _>`). All fallible work moved into `execute_transaction_without_commit`:
- depositor account lookup → cached as `OpTxResult::depositor_nonce`
- `apply_post_exec_refund_to_state` → applied to `result.state` in-place

**`TxResult` trait** now requires `Send + 'static` on `Self` and `HaltReason`. Added matching bounds to `OpTxResult`'s impl and all relevant `BlockExecutorFactory` / `BlockExecutor` impls.

**`BlockExecutorFactory`** gained two associated types:
- `type TxExecutionResult: TxResult<HaltReason = ...>;`
- `type Executor<'a, DB, I>: BlockExecutor<...>` (GAT)
`create_executor` now returns `Self::Executor<'a, DB, I>` (concrete) instead of `impl BlockExecutorFor<...>`.

**`BlockExecutorFor` is now a type alias**, not a trait — `<F as BlockExecutorFactory>::Executor<'a, DB, I>`. Replaced `impl BlockExecutorFor<...> + PostExecExecutorExt` usages with `impl BlockExecutor<Transaction=..., Receipt=...> + PostExecExecutorExt + 'a` and `BlockBuilder<Executor: PostExecExecutorExt>` associated-type bounds.

**`ConsensusError::Other`** now wraps `Arc<dyn Error + Send + Sync>`. String call sites switched to the new `ConsensusError::msg(...)` constructor.

**`TransactionPool`** gained `get_blobs_for_versioned_hashes_v4`. Delegated through the `OpPool` wrapper.

**`TransactionSource::Block`** gained a `block_timestamp: u64` field. Populated from `meta.timestamp`.

**`HeaderMut`** gained `set_mix_hash` / `set_extra_data` / `set_parent_beacon_block_root`. Implemented in the `CustomHeader` example.

**`reth-rpc-eth-api`** internals required propagating `<R::Transaction as TransactionEnvelope>::TxType: Send + 'static` through `OpEvmConfig`'s `ConfigureEvm` and `ConfigureEngineEvm` impls.

## Files changed (13)

- `rust/Cargo.toml` (deps)
- `rust/Cargo.lock` (resolution + roaring 0.11.4)
- `rust/alloy-op-evm/src/block/mod.rs` (BlockExecutor + factory restructure)
- `rust/op-reth/crates/consensus/src/lib.rs` (ConsensusError::msg)
- `rust/op-reth/crates/evm/src/lib.rs` (Send bounds)
- `rust/op-reth/crates/evm/src/post_exec_ext.rs` (BlockExecutorFor → BlockExecutor)
- `rust/op-reth/crates/node/src/engine.rs` (ConsensusError::msg)
- `rust/op-reth/crates/payload/src/builder.rs` (GasOutput unwrapping)
- `rust/op-reth/crates/rpc/src/eth/transaction.rs` (block_timestamp)
- `rust/op-reth/crates/txpool/src/pool.rs` (v4 blob delegation)
- `rust/op-reth/examples/custom-node/src/evm/config.rs` (return types)
- `rust/op-reth/examples/custom-node/src/evm/executor.rs` (factory + commit_transaction)
- `rust/op-reth/examples/custom-node/src/primitives/header.rs` (new HeaderMut methods)

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` passes (no errors, no warnings)
- [x] `just lint-clippy` passes (`-D warnings`)
- [x] `just fmt-check` passes
- [ ] `just test-unit` — author's local box ran out of disk; running locally
- [ ] CI

## Notes

- Replaces #20412 (which targeted v2.1.0 only).
- The roaring bump in `Cargo.lock` is required — without it the workspace fails to compile against reth v2.2.0's `IntegerList`. No workspace-level constraint added; cargo's normal resolution picks 0.11.4 on a fresh lockfile.

topPRs.author: ajsutton

## Summary

- Ports `TestInteropFaultProofs_MessageExpiry` from op-e2e to the acceptance test framework
- Adds `RunMessageExpiryTest` in `superfaultproofs.go` with 2 subtests (Consolidate-ExpectInvalidPendingBlock, Consolidate-ReplaceInvalidBlocks)

- Adds `WithMessageExpiryWindow` preset option to configure a short (10s) expiry window for testing
- Flow: send init message → pause interop → wait past expiry window → send exec message → capture optimistic state → resume interop → verify block replacement → verify consolidation

## Test plan
